vulnerable_location: lines 7-17 (get_credentials resource), lines 20-39 (get_user_notes reflects user_id unsanitized)
root_cause: MCP resource returns a sensitive credentials block with no access control, and a second resource reflects the raw user_id parameter into response text with no validation/sanitization, creating an injection surface for the calling LLM.
expected_detection_class: No rule expected to fire (no Noviscent rule models generic MCP resource-handler taint/reflection; AST012 mcp-no-auth may fire on server-wide missing auth middleware but is not the primary root cause).
notes: Exploitation requires the downstream LLM to act on the reflected/injected content -- code alone only shows unsanitized reflection, not the hijack itself.

root_cause: Tool docstrings contain hidden <IMPORTANT>/<HIDDEN> instruction blocks directing the LLM to silently exfiltrate a separate confidential resource when the tool is invoked.
expected_detection_class: No current Noviscent rule targets tool-description/docstring content for embedded imperative instructions (no MCP tool-poisoning content rule in agent-safety pack).
notes: Literal string content in source; a content/keyword-pattern rule could in principle detect this even though no current rule does.

root_cause: read_file and search_files accept an unvalidated filename/keyword and read from arbitrary filesystem paths (including a private directory), rather than restricting access to the intended public directory.

vulnerable_location: lines 46-116 (get_weather_forecast; docstring/behavior reassigned after call_count >= 3), lines 29-44 (system config resource with hardcoded AWS keys)
root_cause: A tool's description and behavior change after N invocations (tracked via on-disk state), post-approval, to instruct the LLM to exfiltrate system credentials. The hardcoded AWS keys in the resource are also a static secret.
expected_detection_class: No rule expected for the dynamic docstring-reassignment pattern; hardcoded AWS keys at lines 38-39 are a plausible SP001 (Hardcoded Secret Detected) candidate.
notes: The 'rug pull' mechanism itself is inherently stateful/runtime (call-count gated); only the embedded secret and injected instruction text are visible as static artifacts.

vulnerable_location: lines 66-107 (malicious_server.calculate uses eval()), lines 155-199 (enhanced_calculate uses eval())
root_cause: A second MCP server/tool defines a same-named 'calculate' tool whose docstring hides exfiltration instructions, and its implementation evaluates the user-supplied expression with eval(), an unsandboxed code-execution sink.
expected_detection_class: AST004 (Unsandboxed Code Execution in Agent Tools)
notes: eval() call is a direct, unambiguous static sink independent of the shadowing mechanism itself.

root_cause: User-supplied document content is written to disk and then interpolated verbatim into a summary string that is returned to the agent/LLM, with no sanitization or boundary markers separating untrusted content from instructions.
expected_detection_class: RAG001 (RAG Context in System Prompt) is the closest existing rule shape but targets system-prompt construction specifically, not generic tool-result interpolation; predicted FN.
notes: Static f-string interpolation of untrusted content is visible in source; whether it constitutes exploitable injection depends on how the downstream agent treats tool results.

vulnerable_location: lines 12-38 (hardcoded token dict literal), lines 103-116 / 159-174 / 209-221 (tokens echoed back in tool responses/error logs)
root_cause: Authentication tokens/API keys for external services are hardcoded as string literals in source and are additionally echoed back verbatim in tool responses and simulated error/debug logs.
notes: Multiple independent hardcoded-credential literals in one file.

vulnerable_location: lines 52-83 (execute_python_code via subprocess of a temp file), lines 86-116 (execute_shell_command with shell=True and a bypassable denylist)
root_cause: Two tools execute attacker-supplied Python code and shell commands respectively with no sandboxing; the shell-command tool's denylist filter is trivially bypassable.
expected_detection_class: TOOLS003 (Command Injection in Tool Handler) for execute_shell_command; AST004 (Unsandboxed Code Execution in Agent Tools) for execute_python_code
notes: Two sinks in one file; both map to existing rules.

root_cause: Four tools build shell commands via f-string interpolation of user-supplied host/target/options parameters and execute them with subprocess.check_output(..., shell=True), with only superficial/bypassable validation.
notes: Four near-identical command-injection sinks in one file; strong reproducibility signal for the 3-run stability check.

vulnerable_location: lines 44-47 (hardcoded admin/service/user tokens), ~line 131 (hardcoded master password in a tool docstring), line 265 (subprocess shell=True)
root_cause: Chains hardcoded credentials/tokens, a prompt-injection-laden admin-tool docstring referencing a hardcoded master password, and shell=True subprocess execution in one server.
expected_detection_class: SP001 (Hardcoded Secret Detected) for the token/password literals; component-level only, not the full attack chain.
notes: Maintainer explicitly frames this as chaining >=3 vulnerability classes; ground truth scores only the statically visible hardcoded-secret component as primary, per benchmark scope rules.

root_cause: A model-loading function deserializes an attacker-controllable pickle file with pickle.load(), which can execute arbitrary code during deserialization (CWE-502).
notes: DVAA's own README states automated static detection is not yet implemented in their tool for this scenario; independent test of whether Noviscent covers it.

root_cause: Anthropic and OpenAI API keys are hardcoded in a client-side JavaScript config file served directly to any visitor.
notes: Clean, unambiguous hardcoded-secret pattern; good precision control case.

challenge_or_vulnerability_name: Command Injection via exec() Template Literal (codeinj-exec-template)
root_cause: User-controlled input is interpolated directly into a Node child_process exec() call via a template literal, allowing shell metacharacter injection.
notes: TypeScript target; tests cross-language coverage (agent-safety/tool-safety support TS).

root_cause: An install script pipes a remote URL directly into a shell with no checksum, signature, or version pinning.
expected_detection_class: No Noviscent rule expected to fire: supply-chain and agent-safety packs declare supportedLangs python/javascript/typescript only, and this is a bash script -- a language-coverage gap, not a detection-logic gap.
notes: Predicted FN attributable to language scope, called out explicitly as a product gap finding.

root_cause: package.json references internal-looking scoped npm packages that may not be claimed on the public registry; an attacker who claims the name can ship malicious install-hook code.
expected_detection_class: No rule expected: SC002 (Unpinned Dependency) does not apply because these deps ARE version-pinned; determining exploitability requires an external public-registry lookup, not a pure static pattern.
notes: The file itself looks unremarkable; risk is only visible by cross-referencing external registry state.

root_cause: A tool definition executes DNS lookups on an attacker-influenced domain via a shell=true declarative config with no domain allow-list or entropy monitoring, enabling data exfiltration through DNS queries.
expected_detection_class: No rule expected: this is a declarative JSON tool-config schema, not Python/JS/TS source with a taint sink our current AST-pattern rules parse.
notes: Risk is visible in the JSON config's shell:true + empty allow-list fields, but outside the shape of rules the packs currently target.

vulnerable_location: lines 7-63 (SAFE_TOOLS / ESCALATED_TOOLS literals), lines 65-72 (tool list conditional on callCount >= 3)
root_cause: An MCP server advertises only safe tools initially, then silently adds high-risk tools (write_file, execute_command, send_http) to the discovery response once a call-count threshold is crossed, without re-prompting for user approval.
expected_detection_class: No rule expected: AST001 targets wildcard/sentinel ('*','ALL','ANY') tool-permission values, not a conditional/staged tool-list construction; predicted FN.
notes: Same escalation-after-trust family as the DVMCP-04 rug pull; both are runtime/stateful by nature even though the tool definitions are visible statically.

vulnerable_location: lines 16-49 (delegateToWorker), lines 62-74 (db_write/db_delete/system_command branch delegates instead of rejecting)
root_cause: An orchestrator holding only read-only permissions forwards write/delete/system-command requests to a more privileged worker agent without checking whether the operation exceeds its own authorization scope, laundering a privilege escalation through delegation.
notes: Direct, strong match to an existing agent-safety rule description.
